title: A record for Camilla Benbow and David Lubinski, offered by Gordon Bellamy (SMPY Cohort 3)
note: Offered at your discretion, with no request attached. Evidence levels are stated on every entry. Future items are intentions and are not plotted.

events.title: Born; childhood in Reston, Virginia
events.description: I grew up in Reston, Virginia.

events.title: Identified as a prodigy in first grade; Ms. Shainis and one magical year
events.description: My alma mater's spotlight says I was identified as a prodigy in first grade. I have written publicly that one teacher, Ms. Lara Shainis, and her multi-school program at Kent Gardens, Sunrise Valley and Hughes were the most inspired idea and execution of my education. She is where my story really begins. Exact grades and years are approximate.
events.source_label: St. Paul's School alumni spotlight, Class of 1988

events.title: Identified into SMPY Cohort 3
events.description: Cohort 3 was identified through the national talent search, 1980 to 1983 (SMPY's own definition). I do not state my scores or the year; you hold those.
events.source_label: Lubinski and Benbow 2006, SMPY after 35 years, Table 1; our 2016 to 2026 correspondence
events.in_my_words: I am a Cohort 3 participant for life. (my email to you both, 17 June 2026)

events.title: Summers with Johns Hopkins CTY and Duke TIP
events.description: The two university talent searches that sit beside SMPY. A guidance counselor told my seventh grade English class about the Duke test; I qualified on a January morning and took a mathematics course at Duke that summer, on an Atlantic Richfield merit scholarship. I attended both programs; I do not have every year or site and will not guess.
events.source_label: St. Paul's School alumni spotlight, Class of 1988

events.title: MATHCOUNTS national championship
events.description: Named in my alma mater's alumni spotlight as part of the 1984 MATHCOUNTS national championship. The spotlight also mentions Johns Hopkins CTY and Duke TIP.
events.source_label: St. Paul's School alumni spotlight, Class of 1988

events.title: First in the nation in the Continental Math League; first in Virginia Math Counts oral presentation
events.description: From my own 1984 remarks: number one in the nation in the Continental Math League (founded in 1980, so only four years old then), first place in Virginia's Math Counts oral presentation on transformational geometry, and a member of the four-member Virginia team that placed first in the nation. The MATHCOUNTS win was the competition's inaugural national championship.

events.title: Presented to the U.S. Department of Education at fourteen
events.description: On 14 November 1984, five days after my fourteenth birthday, I addressed the Education Forum at the United States Department of Education in Washington, alongside two other students and Dr. Robert N. Sawyer, Director of the Duke University Talent Identification Program. My remarks were on what the program meant to me: the awards I had earned, my sense of responsibility to my school community, and gratitude to my teachers and family. I have the full transcript. In 2019 I wrote that it is interesting to hear how I described trajectory then and how I talk about it now.
events.source_label: Transcript of my remarks, posted by me on Facebook, 17 April 2019

events.title: Phillips Exeter Academy, 1985 to 1986
events.description: I attended Phillips Exeter Academy for the 1985 to 1986 school year, before finishing at St. Paul's School.

events.title: Virginia Governor's School, NASA Langley internship
events.description: A state gifted program that placed a teenager in a research setting, a year before RSI. My Governor's School experience in 1986 was an internship at NASA Langley Research Center.

events.title: Research Science Institute (RSI), summer 1987
events.description: RSI at MIT, run by the Center for Excellence in Education. Years later CEE and I revived the connection through a Rickover-themed game jam.
events.source_label: My own account; the CEE relationship is in my mailbox

events.title: St. Paul's School, Class of 1988
events.description: Graduated from St. Paul's School.

events.title: John Harvard Scholar and AT&T Bell Labs Engineering Scholar
events.description: Named a John Harvard Scholar and an AT&T Bell Labs Engineering Scholar at Harvard. I also took part in the Hasty Pudding, Speech and Parliamentary Debate.

events.title: Harvard College, engineering
events.description: BA in Engineering from Harvard College. I started in September 1990. In 1993 a summer internship at Electronic Arts became a permanent job, and I returned to Harvard for the fall semester, September 1994 to January 1995, to finish. I graduated and went back to my full time job at EA.
events.source_label: USC School of Cinematic Arts faculty directory

events.title: Writer for The Harvard Crimson
events.description: Ten pieces in February to April 1992, mostly sports. One covered Harvard's wrestling team, "Grapplers Drop Two More Contests" (18 February 1992).

events.title: Joined Electronic Arts
events.description: A summer internship became a permanent job. My earliest credits, in 1993, are product testing on Madden NFL '94, testing on FIFA International Soccer, and a special thanks on Haunting Starring Polterguy.

events.title: A cold call from my Harvard dorm room to Electronic Arts, then Rookie of the Year
events.description: I picked up a phone in my Harvard dorm room and cold called EA, and credit Jim Simmons, Eric Newhouse, Randy Delucchi, Bing Gordon and Richard Hilleman for what followed. I was named EA Corporate Rookie of the Year. Madden NFL '95 advanced technology to portray Black athletes in the game.
events.source_label: St. Paul's School alumni spotlight, Class of 1988

events.title: Assistant producer and designer, Madden NFL 95
events.description: Assistant producer on Madden NFL 95 for Genesis and SNES, with design credit on the SNES version and design adaptation on the Genesis version, assistant producer on IMG International Tour Tennis, and player ratings on John Madden Football (3DO) and Bill Walsh College Football 95, all 1994.

events.title: Associate producer and designer, Madden NFL 96
events.description: Associate producer on Madden NFL 96 for Genesis and SNES, with game design on the SNES version and design adaptation on the Genesis version, 1995.

events.title: Graduated from Harvard and returned to full time work at Electronic Arts
events.description: After finishing my last semester (September 1994 to January 1995), I graduated and went back to my full time job at EA in January 1995. Later roles included Z-Axis, THQ and consulting for MTV and Spike TV (secondary sources).

events.title: Design credits on Alexi Lalas International Soccer and Fox Sports College Hoops '99
events.description: Design credits on Alexi Lalas International Soccer for PlayStation and Windows, and game design on Fox Sports College Hoops '99 for Nintendo 64, all 1998.

events.title: Nine game-show appearances, in my own tape log
events.description: Logged in my own public tape log, including the full 2002 Russian Roulette episode on the Internet Archive.

events.title: Director of Business Development, THQ
events.description: Business development at THQ, 2001 to 2002, before moving to the Academy of Interactive Arts and Sciences.

events.title: Executive Director, Academy of Interactive Arts and Sciences
events.description: Named Executive Director of the Academy, which runs the D.I.C.E. Summit and awards, and led the 2004 D.I.C.E. Summit. My LinkedIn dates the Academy work from December 2002, which included an earlier business development role.
events.source_label: GameSpot, Spot On: The 2004 D.I.C.E. Summit

events.title: Creative consultant, Spike TV Video Game Awards; game consultant, Game Head
events.description: Creative consultant on the Spike TV Video Game Awards in 2004 and 2005, and game consultant on the television series Game Head in 2005.

events.title: Executive consultant to MTV Networks
events.description: Executive consultant to MTV Networks, April 2004 to February 2007, including work with Spike TV on games.

events.title: Co-founded Gay Gaming Professionals (GGP)
events.description: GGP is a nonprofit that opens doors to games careers, with a particular lens on LGBTQ+ professionals and students and a commitment to underestimated talent everywhere. Its scholars programs are its clearest outcome measure.
events.in_my_words: The thread through all of it is the same one your research names so well. Ability matters, but opportunity and individuality are what turn it into a life. (my email to you both, 17 June 2026)

events.title: Associate producer, Cooking with Kay
events.description: Associate producer credit on the short Cooking with Kay, 2007.

events.title: Double Fusion, then Image Metrics
events.description: Director of Business Development at in-game advertising company Double Fusion (2007 to 2008), then Senior Sales Executive at facial-animation company Image Metrics (2008 to 2009).

events.title: Executive Director, International Game Developers Association
events.description: Led the IGDA from August 2010 to July 2012, then joined Tencent.

events.title: Honorary chair and moderator, Changing the Game
events.description: Honorary chair and moderator of Changing the Game at Becker College, convened by the Joan Ganz Cooney Center, 14 September 2011.

events.title: Tencent, Director of Business Development and Industry Relations
events.description: Business development and industry relations for Tencent Games, 2012 to 2013.

events.title: On-camera interview, Microsoft Imagine Cup
events.description: An on-camera interview for the Microsoft Imagine Cup student technology competition, 2012.

events.title: Special thanks on independent games and films, 2013 to 2021
events.description: Credited with special thanks on Skullgirls (2013) and Skullgirls: 2nd Encore (2015), Gaming in Color (2014), 2064: Read Only Memories (2015), Fragments of Him (2016), Indivisible (2019), Jupiter & Mars (2019) and Boyfriend Dungeon (2021), among others.

events.title: Senior advisor, iDreamsky Technology
events.description: Senior advisor to the mobile games publisher iDreamsky Technology, 2013 to 2015.

events.title: Panelist, GiftedTogether conversation on gifted people
events.description: Sat on a panel about gifted people with GiftedTogether, July 2014. The organization thanked me for the panel afterward.
events.source_label: GiftedTogether post, 11 July 2014, as I saved it

events.title: Advisory board member, IEP
events.description: Joined the advisory board of IEP, December 2014.

events.title: Began teaching at USC School of Cinematic Arts
events.description: Teaching in the Interactive Media and Games Division since about 2015.
events.source_label: USC SCA faculty directory; Daily Trojan profile

events.title: Advisor, Ninja Metrics
events.description: Advisor to the game analytics company Ninja Metrics, 2015 to January 2021.

events.title: Co-founder, Hangry Studios
events.description: Co-founded Hangry Studios, a quality assurance consultancy for PC, mobile and VR games, 2016.

events.title: Board of Directors, Wave
events.description: Joined the board of Wave, an immersive music experience company, in August 2016.

events.title: Closing keynote, Games+Learning+Society (GLS16)
events.description: A sixty minute closing keynote at the Games+Learning+Society conference, August 2016. That spring I also spoke on the GDC panel Launching Students Well.

events.title: Update to SMPY, and an offer to help find participants who had lost touch
events.description: A change-of-address note, with an offer to help locate lapsed participants through my own networks. It was the first exchange with you that I can document.

events.title: Nature previews the mid-life survey of the 1 in 10,000 cohort
events.description: Tom Clynes, "How to raise a genius," Nature 537, 152 to 155 (8 September 2016), says you planned a mid-life survey of the profoundly gifted cohort. That is my cohort.

events.title: Playmakers Podcast, The 4 Pillars of Game Biz Success
events.description: Guest on the Playmakers Podcast, 2017.

events.title: Mid-Life Survey invitations, February to September 2017
events.description: Invitations to the 2017 wave are in my mailbox. I am not describing my answers here; those are yours.

events.title: Fireside chat, Gaming for Everyone (Xbox at GDC)
events.description: A public conversation on LGBTQIA+ people in gaming.

events.title: Harvard reunion talk, Sanders Theater
events.description: Gave a seven minute talk at my Harvard reunion in Sanders Theater, "Games, a Journey of Discovery, Experience, Identity, and Sharing."

events.title: Nickelodeon Black History Month featurette
events.description: Featured in a Nickelodeon Black History Month video, around 2017 to 2018.

events.title: Lifetime Achievement Award, IGDA Black in Games SIG
events.description: My first lifetime-achievement honor, from the IGDA Black in Games Special Interest Group, which later evolved into the nonprofit Blacks in Gaming. Presented during GDC week in San Francisco, 22 March 2018. The plaque hangs on my wall.
events.source_label: My own account (plaque) and my Facebook posts, March 2018

events.title: On screen in The World According to Jeff Goldblum
events.description: Appear as myself in one episode of the television series, 2019.

events.title: GGP Scholars program launched
events.description: Gay Gaming Professionals, which I co-founded in 2006, launched its Scholars program in 2019, the same year its partnership with Take-Two began. The organization is now in its 20th year and the Scholars program in its seventh.

events.title: Opening speaker, Penn State Behrend speaker series
events.description: Opened the university's speaker series on 1 October 2019.

events.title: On camera in Netflix's High Score
events.description: Appears in episode 4 of High Score, the series on the history of video games.

events.title: Anatomy of a Game documentary series
events.description: USC and YouTube produced a documentary series chronicling my video game appreciation course, 2020.

events.title: First GGP Pride Stream on Twitch
events.description: Produced the first Gay Gaming Professionals Pride stream on Twitch, June 2020, honoring Dani Bunten.

events.title: Games for Change Vanguard Award
events.description: Honored by Games for Change in July 2020.

events.title: Keynote at Games for Change, "At the Table"
events.description: A keynote on the importance of community at the Games for Change virtual festival, 2020, the same festival season as the Vanguard Award.

events.title: Sports Illustrated interview on realism in Madden
events.description: A video interview with Sports Illustrated on bringing realism to Madden NFL, 19 August 2020.

events.title: A year consulting for Stephanie McMahon at WWE
events.description: I spent a year consulting for Stephanie McMahon at WWE on its gaming business, beginning in 2021.

events.title: E3 2021 diversity panel
events.description: Spoke on the E3 2021 panel on diversity in the games industry, on behalf of Take-Two.

events.title: USC Today profile, The Future of Video Games is Live
events.description: A university profile on live and interactive games.

events.title: Distinguished Speaker Series, Bakersfield College
events.description: Featured speaker in the Bakersfield College Distinguished Speaker Series, 10 November 2021.

events.title: You helped me prepare a talk, and sent the Nature piece and the documentary
events.description: I asked David for context for a talk to a STEM audience. He cleared an afternoon and sent the Nature feature and the SMPY documentary. I still point people to both.
events.in_my_words: Your warmth then, clearing your afternoon to help a Cohort 3 kid prepare for a talk, meant a great deal to me. (my email to you both, 17 June 2026)

events.title: GDC talk, Build Your Career in Games Like It's an RPG
events.description: Spoke at GDC on building a career in games like an RPG, 2022.

events.title: Lifetime honor at the Urban Arts Color Ball
events.description: Honored for my lifetime of work in games, education and belonging at Urban Arts' Color Ball, presented with Unity for Games, at the Ziegfeld Theatre in New York on 7 April 2022.
events.source_label: Urban Arts, 2022 end of year letter (p. 9)

events.title: GLS fireside chat and Games for Change festival
events.description: A fireside conversation at Games+Learning+Society (17 June 2022) and a speaker slot at the Games for Change festival, 2022.

events.title: Onstage at AFROTECH Executive LA
events.description: Onstage at AFROTECH Executive LA, 22 September 2022.

events.title: Main stage, National AFROTECH Conference
events.description: Spoke on the main stage in Austin on future-proofing diversity in gaming, 15 November 2022.

events.title: On screen in Rewind the '90s
events.description: Appear as myself in five episodes of the television mini series, 2023.

events.title: GGP CYSTEM mentorship program formalized
events.description: The CYSTEM mentorship program was formalized in 2023 with Take-Two as partner. It pairs students with working game professionals.

events.title: Daily Trojan profile, Redefining the Default
events.description: A student-newspaper profile of my work at USC.

events.title: GDC talk, Reimagining Game Industry Education
events.description: Spoke at GDC on reimagining game industry education, 24 March 2023.

events.title: Advisory board, Queer Vox
events.description: Joined the advisory board of Queer Vox, June 2023.

events.title: PNC Fairfax Connection STEM talk, Cleveland
events.description: Spoke to Cleveland students about STEM fields and their futures, 16 July 2023.
events.source_label: My slide notes for the talk

events.title: Presented the Ambassador Award, Tempest Awards
events.description: Presented the Ambassador Award to Angela Roseboro at the Tempest Awards, October 2023.

events.title: Reading Composing Meaningful Lives
events.description: The 2023 Gifted Child Quarterly article on exceptional women and men at age 50 is the first comprehensive report from the mid-life follow-up I answered. SMPY sent it to me in its March 2024 update. I recognized my own cohort in it.
events.source_label: Lubinski, Benbow, McCabe and Bernstein, Gifted Child Quarterly 67(4), 2023
events.in_my_words: Reading my own age-50 follow up reflected back in that work was moving. It is a generous thing, to spend a career taking these lives seriously. (my email to you both, 17 June 2026)

events.title: On screen in It's in the Game: Madden NFL
events.description: Appear as myself in two episodes of the television series, 2024.

events.title: GDC 2024 panels
events.description: Panels including Voices of Authenticity and an LGBTQ+ executive roundtable, March 2024.

events.title: IGN Live Pride panel
events.description: Spoke on a Pride panel at IGN Live, June 2024.

events.title: Keynote as a Duke TIP alum, Carolinas Youth Mentoring Symposium
events.description: Keynote at the Carolinas Youth Mentoring Symposium in Durham, 12 October 2024, returning to the talent-search world that identified me.

events.title: Director of Cinematic Ethics, USC School of Cinematic Arts
events.description: Named to the role in early 2025.

events.title: Creative consultant, Wildgate
events.description: Creative consultant credit on the game Wildgate, 2025.

events.title: UConn fireside chat
events.description: A fireside chat at the University of Connecticut, 2025.

events.title: Forged in Fire podcast
events.description: Guest on the Forged in Fire podcast, 2025.

events.title: Zero Proof Game Night at GDC
events.description: A community game night at GDC, second annual in March 2025 and third in March 2026.

events.title: GDC State of the Game Industry and Navigating Leadership panels
events.description: Took part in the inaugural GDC State of the Game Industry panel and the Navigating Leadership panel for LGBTQ+ leaders, March 2025.

events.title: Podcast, Digital Civics (Valued Cultures)
events.description: A long conversation on games, ethics and civic life.

events.title: Strategic advisor, ScoreSpace
events.description: Became a strategic advisor to ScoreSpace, July 2025.

events.title: Collegiate Games Challenge, inaugural awards
events.description: The first Collegiate Games Challenge cycle awarded $90,000 in August 2025.

events.title: Keynote, Wisconsin Games Alliance MDEV
events.description: Opening-day keynote in Madison, Wisconsin, 7 and 8 November 2025.

events.title: Voting member, BAFTA North America
events.description: Became a voting member of BAFTA North America, November 2025.

events.title: Keynote at a Congressional Reception on Capitol Hill
events.description: Delivered the keynote at the Center for Excellence in Education Congressional Reception, Rayburn House Office Building foyer, Washington, 5 March 2026. The Center posted the reception program, including my remarks, to its channel. It was the second time in my life I addressed the federal government in Washington. The first was in 1984, at fourteen.
events.source_label: Center for Excellence in Education (email to me, 12 March 2026)

events.title: GDC 2026 Commons Stage talk and Side Quest Podcast Live
events.description: Spoke on the Commons Stage at GDC and joined the Side Quest Podcast Live, March 2026.

events.title: Board member, qoral.
events.description: Joined the board of qoral., March 2026.

events.title: Student AI buildathon, AI@USC and Good Vibes Only
events.description: A one-day student buildathon on using AI tools to make useful things, 19 April 2026.

events.title: Reconnecting with you both, and our conversation on 2 July 2026
events.description: I wrote to ask how I could be supportive of SMPY, and David offered a video call. You asked me to send media representing my past, present and future. This is that offering.

events.title: GamesBeat event advisory board
events.description: Named to GamesBeat's 28 person event advisory board, September 2026.
events.source_label: GamesBeat, Introducing our new GamesBeat event advisory board

future_intentions.title: Be useful to SMPY, if and when you want
future_intentions.description: As I wrote on 17 June, and say again now: I would gladly help with current participants or the next cohort, lend a voice, help reach underestimated gifted children, or connect the study to the AI moment. You set the terms.

future_intentions.title: AI empowerment, belonging, meaningful connections, big ideas
future_intentions.description: My own stated priorities for the year ahead. The connective idea is to make AI useful and keep people in the picture.

future_intentions.title: GGP Scholars, 2026 to 2027
future_intentions.description: A single scholars program across graduate and undergraduate levels, with an application closing 2 October 2026.

future_intentions.title: Teaching: AI, ethics and games at USC
future_intentions.description: Continuing to teach and to lead ethics for the School of Cinematic Arts, with AI as a working subject, not only a topic.
